title: Gold Leaf Mistake
subject: A shop-front sign-writer gilds the name of a new bakery in gold leaf, spells it wrong, and the owner keeps it because queues form to point at it
caption: Acid jazz, 1990s London club session sound. Rhodes electric piano playing syncopated minor-seventh chords, wah-wah rhythm guitar chopping on the offbeats, trumpet and tenor sax horn stabs on the chorus, round slap-leaning electric bass, tight live drums with ghost-note snare, congas. Dry punchy drums, wide Rhodes, tight horn section. Male lead voice, smooth and clear, female backing pair answering. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 108 BPM, D minor. Cheeky and groovy. No Hammond organ, no synth leads, no autotune, no rapping, no four-on-the-floor EDM kick.
lyrics:
[Intro - Rhodes, wah guitar, conga]

[Verse 1]
Brush in my hand at seven in the morning
Gold leaf lifting off the book
Baker wants his name across the window
Bread and Butter, but I wrote Breed

[Pre-Chorus]
Steady hand, steady hand
One long breath, then it's dry

[Chorus]
Breed and butter, breed and butter
Look what I've gone and done
Now the queue goes round the corner
Everybody's pointing up

[Verse 2]
I came back with my turpentine
The baker said leave it, it's perfect
He sold out before the noon

[Chorus]
Breed and butter, breed and butter
Look what I've gone and done
He's paid me twice the fee
Gold is gold and wrong is right

[Bridge - horns, drums break]
One letter, one letter
Now it's on a postcard

[Chorus]
Breed and butter, breed and butter
Look what I've gone and done
Better than the proper one
Everybody's pointing up

[Outro - wah guitar, Rhodes vamp]
Breed and butter
Breed and butter
